title: A Ghost for the Cover
premise: Mirabel Thackeray, a private security contractor whose firm guards clients too compromised for anyone else, is approached by a stranger named Callum Voss who claims she once saved his life — a favor she has no memory of. The debt he repays drags her into an operation to extract Dr. Elena Sarkissian, a defector carrying evidence that a powerful consortium has been laundering influence through the very summit Mirabel's company is contracted to protect. As Mirabel realizes the defector may be bait designed to flush out and destroy everyone who knows the truth — including her own employer — she must choose between the duty that defines her and the growing bond with Voss, who may not be who he claims. In the end, Mirabel exposes the consortium at the summit itself, sacrifices her career and cover identity, and escapes with Voss and Sarkissian, finally owning an identity of her own making.
about_author: Isandro Halloran is the pen name of a former risk consultant who spent a decade advising security firms in politically unstable markets before turning to fiction. Halloran writes thrillers about people caught between institutions and their own consciences, drawing on a life spent watching power negotiate with truth.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Mirabel Thackeray's POV. Between contracts in Vienna, she runs background checks on clients nobody trusts, following rules that keep shifting beneath her. A stranger, Callum Voss, corners her at a café and insists she saved his life in Marseilles three years ago — a city she never worked. He leaves a keycard and a warning. Emotional beat: unease; her ordered world develops its first crack.

chapters.title: Terms of Indebtedness
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. He explains the debt: someone used Mirabel's name and credentials to smuggle a package out of Marseilles, saving his network but implicating her. Now the consortium that owns her firm wants the loose ends cut. He offers her a way out that requires helping him extract defector Dr. Elena Sarkissian before the Geneva summit. Beat: reluctant bargain struck under mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: House Rules
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She returns to her firm, Meridian Protective Services, and finds her access quietly restricted — someone above her already knows. Her handler, Director Anselm Roth, assigns her to the summit security detail with suspicious warmth. She copies what she can and lies well for the first time. Beat: the vertigo of realizing the institution she served was never on her side.

chapters.title: The Defector's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Sarkissian's POV, in hiding outside Zurich. Elena weighs defection against the knowledge that whoever extracts her controls her evidence — proof the consortium laundered billions through defense contracts feeding the summit's host government. She suspects she is bait. She sends a coded message offering herself only to Mirabel by name. Beat: cold clarity; the hunted choosing her hunter.

chapters.title: Rewritten Rules
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Roth briefs the summit detail and names Sarkissian as a hostile asset to be 'contained on contact.' Mirabel recognizes the order as a death warrant dressed as protocol. She meets Voss at night on the lakefront and agrees to run the extraction herself. Beat: the point of no return crossed quietly, almost bureaucratically.

chapters.title: Marseille, Reconstructed
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Voss walks Mirabel through reconstructed records of the Marseilles op, and fragments surface — a blackout week, a burned passport, a version of herself she doesn't remember being. Either her memory was edited or Voss is building a fiction around her. Beat: identity destabilized; love and manipulation becoming indistinguishable.

chapters.title: The Containment Order
chapters.summary: Roth's POV. Inside Meridian, we see the machinery of corruption: Roth reports to consortium fixer Ilse Brandt, who wants Sarkissian taken alive long enough to be discredited publicly, then gone. Roth flags Mirabel's data access. He gives her a partner, taciturn operative Dane Okonkwo, explicitly to watch her. Beat: dread from the predator's side of the glass.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Mirabel and Voss's POV, alternating. They plan the extraction in a shuttered hotel, counting exits, timers, betrayals. Working together, the suspicion between them thins into something warmer — shared coffee at 3 a.m., laughter that surprises them both. Mirabel admits she can't remember who she was before Meridian. Beat: intimacy growing inside operational discipline.

chapters.title: Okonkwo's Report
chapters.summary: Dane's POV. Ordered to surveil Mirabel, Dane instead finds evidence she's right: the containment order violates every rulebook he's ever followed. Torn between loyalty and conscience, he deletes one incriminating log entry — his first small treason. Beat: a good soldier discovering the orders were the enemy all along.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Sarkissian's POV. Mirabel makes contact through Elena's dead-drop, proving her identity with the Marseilles keycard — which Elena recognizes. Elena reveals the keycard belonged to the courier who actually ran the favor: someone inside Meridian framed Mirabel deliberately, years ago, as a pre-built scapegoat. Beat: revelation reframing everything; Mirabel was chosen before she ever chose.

chapters.title: The Bait Question
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. If the frame was planned, the extraction may be too — the consortium may want Sarkissian moved so they can catch everyone involved at once. Voss argues they proceed anyway; Mirabel suspects Voss's own agenda isn't clean. First real fight between them, sharp and honest. Beat: trust tested by logic; love refusing to be naive.

chapters.title: Geneva Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Summit week begins; the city fills with delegations, drones, and Meridian's gray-suited details. Brandt arrives personally. Roth hands Mirabel the summit floor plan — and watches her memorize the wrong parts. Beat: tightening vise; every professional courtesy now a trap being set.

chapters.title: Extraction: Leg One
chapters.summary: Mirabel and Voss's POV. They lift Sarkissian from her Zurich safehouse during a scheduled power maintenance window, moving her through freight tunnels. It works — too cleanly. Mirabel clocks the absent surveillance and realizes someone let them through. Beat: adrenaline curdling into certainty that they're running down a corridor built for them.

chapters.title: What Voss Owes
chapters.summary: Voss's POV, confession. Voss admits he wasn't saved by Mirabel — he was saved by the courier who used her name, a woman he loved, now dead. Helping Mirabel is both penance and a way to finish what the courier started. Mirabel, furious, then honest, chooses to continue with eyes open. Beat: betrayal transmuted into a harder, truer intimacy.

chapters.title: Dane's Choice
chapters.summary: Dane's POV. Roth orders Dane to shadow the extraction team and signal positions. Instead Dane feeds Roth a false route and joins Mirabel at a rail yard, bringing Meridian's internal comms codes. Beat: the institution loses its last honest instrument; three fugitives become four.

chapters.title: Brandt Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Ilse springs the countertrap: Sarkissian's evidence cache is seeded with a tracker, and Meridian declares Mirabel a rogue operative, burning her identity across every database she's ever touched. Her bank accounts, licenses, history — erased. Beat: total exposure; the theme of identity made literal and violent.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Stripped of every credential, Mirabel becomes exactly what the title promises — a ghost. Using the courier's old Marseilles tradecraft, recovered from Voss's records, the team moves Sarkissian toward Geneva under summit chaos as cover. Beat: liberation inside loss; without a file, she is finally free to author herself.

chapters.title: The Summit Floor
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The team infiltrates the summit as contractors, planning to broadcast Sarkissian's evidence on the delegation feed rather than flee with it. Roth spots Mirabel in a service corridor and, instead of raising alarm, hesitates — his own survival math has changed. Beat: coiled tension; the heist begins amid the world's most watched room.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Mirabel and Sarkissian's POV. Elena reaches the media uplink as Brandt's men close in; Dane holds the corridor, Voss the roof. The evidence goes live mid-session — contracts, accounts, names. Roth, cornered, chooses to delay the response teams rather than die protecting Brandt. Beat: climax ignites; truth deployed as a weapon.

chapters.title: Ilse Brandt's Exit
chapters.summary: Brandt and Mirabel's POV, converging. Brandt nearly escapes by helicopter but Mirabel intercepts her with the one thing money can't buy back: the recording of Brandt ordering the containment kill. Security services, suddenly very interested, take Brandt into custody as her patrons disown her. Beat: corrupt power devoured by its own machinery.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Unlisted
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Meridian collapses into scandal; Roth testifies quietly for immunity; Dane disappears into a new life. Mirabel, legally nonexistent, sits with Voss and Sarkissian in a Marseille harbor café — the city where the false favor began — deciding what to build from nothing. Beat: grief and relief braided together; the cost counted honestly.

chapters.title: A Ghost for the Cover
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, final. Offered new papers under a new name by a grateful intelligence contact, Mirabel instead writes her own: she keeps Thackeray, but on terms she sets, founding a two-person consultancy with Voss that takes only clients she can look in the eye. Elena publishes; the summit convenes under a cleaner light. Final beat: love against duty resolved — she chooses both, on her own authority, no longer anyone's ghost.
